metadata.name: Washington State Aviation Grant Prioritization
metadata.agency: Washington State Department of Transportation (WSDOT), Aviation Division
metadata.source_citation: ACRP Synthesis 123 (2023), Chapter 4 — State of Washington case example, pp. 41-42. Sourced from interview with David Fleckenstein, Director of Aviation, WSDOT, May 6, 2022. ACRP notes Washington uses all 11 evaluation criteria from the synthesis survey and includes statutory criteria, weighted scoring, with statute dictating award rules but not prioritization methodology.

decisions_log.author: APH m49 Sprint 6 reference encoder
decisions_log.decision: Encoded Washington as additive_100pt model with 11 criteria mirroring the full ACRP 11-factor list, plus two set-asides (10% transformation/sustainability, 25% non-NPIAS).
decisions_log.rationale: ACRP Syn 123 documents Washington uses 'a spreadsheet with formulas and all 11 evaluation criteria.' The 10% airport-transformation-grant set-aside (established 2019) and 25% non-NPIAS allocation are unique features; encoded as set_asides.

criteria.label: Regulatory Mandate
criteria.description: Project addresses a regulatory mandate or compliance directive.

subcategories.label: Mandated by statute or FAA directive

criteria.label: Safety
criteria.description: Project addresses safety deficiencies or enhancements.

criteria.label: Security
criteria.description: Project addresses physical or cyber security.

criteria.label: Customer Service / Capacity
criteria.description: Improves level of service or addresses capacity.

criteria.label: Airport Size
criteria.description: Recognizes airport tier per WSDOT system plan.

criteria.label: Revenue Generation / Cost Reduction
criteria.description: Project generates revenue or reduces operating costs (Washington supports this with its Community Aviation Revitalization Board revolving loan program).

subcategories.label: Strong revenue generation or cost reduction

criteria.label: Environmental / Community Benefit
criteria.description: Environmental or community benefits and impacts.

criteria.label: Sustainability / Airport Transformation
criteria.description: Washington reserves 10% of grant funds for airport transformation grants targeting solar, LED conversion, EV infrastructure, electrical-service ducts, and other sustainability projects.

criteria.label: Asset Preservation
criteria.description: Maintains existing facilities. Washington has prioritized pavement preservation as 'most funds are going toward pavement preservation' per ACRP.

criteria.label: Contribution to Agency / System Plan Goals
criteria.description: Advances WSDOT goals or Washington State Aviation System Plan goals.

subcategories.label: Advances a Washington State Aviation System Plan goal

criteria.label: Risk Factors
criteria.description: Environmental, financial, schedule, or operational risk factors associated with NOT doing the project.

set_asides.label: Airport Transformation Grants (Sustainability)
set_asides.eligibility_filter: Sustainability projects: solar, LED conversion, electric vehicle infrastructure, duct work for future electrical service.

set_asides.label: Non-NPIAS Airports
set_asides.eligibility_filter: Airports not in the National Plan of Integrated Airport Systems.

governance.decision_authority: WSDOT Aviation Division, Director of Aviation
governance.statute_citation: Washington statute dictates how grants are awarded but does not dictate the prioritization process.
governance.approval_process: Grants Program Manager collects all grant requests in a spreadsheet with formulas, scores them against all 11 evaluation criteria, then discusses with the Director of Aviation. One process used for all grants. Director adjusts based on amount of funding available.

disclaimer: Encoding mirrors ACRP Synthesis 123 (2023) summary of Washington's 11-criterion process. Per-criterion point allocations are inferred from typical practice; ACRP does not publish WSDOT's exact spreadsheet weights. The 10% transformation set-aside and 25% non-NPIAS share are documented. Verify against WSDOT Aviation's current grant solicitation before adoption.
